findings.reason: the §2 candidate-census cutover node must name every census polisher as either the authority or a caller; retiring _refine_selected_vertices without reconciling polish_census_stationary_points leaves the single-authority contract unowned.
findings.text: polish_census_stationary_points is a second public position authority built on the same polish_stationary_points kernel (it calls it internally) and is consumed by nova/equilibrium/topology.py:1285 and :1296 for structured census nulls. The plan §2 describes the census position authority as stencil_nulls.xpoint_candidates whose local quadratic _refine_selected_vertices (still live at nova/equilibrium/stencil_nulls.py:1877,1940) "stops being the position authority", and never names polish_census_stationary_points. The design's "one kernel serves three call sites, one position authority" is therefore not what the tree holds.

findings.reason: it contains the design-warning anti-pattern (ranking-based boundary selection on grid flux) but lives outside the two banks §4 regenerates, so naming it would widen the plan rather than correct it.
findings.text: _solved_boundary selects the closed boundary by largest-area contourpy loop on grid flux, a parallel boundary-selection authority carrying the grid-resolution contour the plan §1 says must stop; but this benchmark appears outside the two EFIT banks (MAST corroboration, DIII-D preregistered match) that §4 scoped.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 hides Newton, custom_root implicit differentiation and fixed-slot masking behind one kernel; §3 hides graph assembly, saddle splitting and component classification behind one function; §4 is one dataclass plus one function. Verified in the tree: the shipped forms are deep, not a spread of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 names stencil_nulls.xpoint_candidates as the sole census boundary, while a second spline position authority for census-selected nulls, polish_census_stationary_points, exists and is not named by the plan.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites its reuse map (25 candidates over nova and imas-ambix; docs/figures/efit-baseline-demonstration/reuse-map.md is present) and names the existing mechanism each proposal extends. The public polish kernel is reachable at nova/equilibrium/flux_surface_connectivity.py:916, the branch assembler at nova/equilibrium/separatrix_branches.py:269 (assemble_separatrix_branches), and the shared comparator at nova/equilibrium/boundary_comparison.py:140, so the design builds on what it names.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no proposal adds a thin layer over machinery that should instead be extended. §4 is the right direction: the DIII-D harness element at benchmarks/diiid_forward_gs_match.py:1426 now delegates to assemble_separatrix_branches rather than carrying its own contour selection, which is the replacement the section claims.
